To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
shear-thinning aqueously dispersed polymer solutions exhibit a complex behaviour when used as displacing fluids in immiscible two-phase displacement experiments.
the effects on residual oil formation of shear-thinning polymer solutions are strongly related to the polymer concentrations.

the shear-thinning behaviour of the aqueous polymer solutions used in this work influences the values of the dimensionless capillarity and viscosity numbers, which in turn affects the residual oil saturation, and the size of the residual oil blobs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of shear-thinning displacing fluids on the residual oil formation in pore networks.
the effects of shear-thinning polymer solutions on the displacement dynamics and the residual oil recovery in microfluidic porous media.
the effect of the polymer concentration on the recovery efficiency of the trapped phase and the relationship between the capillary and viscouseffects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shear-thinning behaviour of the displacing fluid has an important effect on the residual oil formation in micromodel experiments, which is related to the values of Ca.
the shear-thinning effect is not the only factor that influences the recovery efficiency and the size distribution.
the shear-thinning behaviour of the polymer solution has a strong effect on the residual oil formation, and the degree of influence depends on the concentration of the polymer solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of shear-thinning displacing fluids, a higher concentration of polymer solution leads to a more viscous displacing fluid (higher M) and to a more favourable displacement (lower Ca).
, in microfluidic networks, shear-thinning fluids can be used to improve oil recovery by increasing the amount of residual oil.
the recovery of residual oil is not affected by the shear-thinning behaviour of the displacing fluid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shear-thinning fluids exhibit a different response to the capillary and viscously driven flow regimes than Newtonian fluids.
the interdependence between M, Ca and the polymer concentration must be considered when interpreting displacement experiments in microfluidic devices.
the use of shear-thinning solutions as displacing fluid in porous media experiments requires careful interpretation of the experimental results in terms of capillary and viscose forces.
